cv.scheme: group_time rolling-origin backtest (panel, not sklearn CV)

noise_floor_definition: sd of MASE across the 5 backtest origins (origin-to-origin spread), used for paired per-origin comparisons
fixed_steps: sales == -1 -> NaN (impossible negative sales), interpolated within each series' own history
inventory_end excluded from all features (same-period leak, also unavailable for the future)
holiday_week reproduced from calendar rule (ISO week-of-year in {1,14,27,47,51,52}) for gap rows and the future horizon
promo = 0 (ASSUMED baseline scenario) for the future horizon; no promotion calendar supplied

stages.pick_reason: tied with AutoTheta and naive_last on the backtest (paired diffs << paired SE across 5 origins) but the only candidate using known-in-advance promo/holiday_week covariates, and the actual 8-week delivered window is unusually holiday-dense (3/8 weeks) with measured +18%/+24% median uplifts; confirmed on the frozen test set: MASE 0.992 vs seasonal_naive 1.143 and naive_last 1.252
